I. 
Background Information: 
 
What in Earth-soil helps plants grow? 
 
 
The three main nutrients that Earth-soil has are nitrogen (N), 
phosphorous (P), and potassium (K). Soil possesses recycled nutrients, 
including carbon. Plants also need small quantities of iron, manganese, 
zinc, copper, boron, molybdenum. These facts was from the Department of 
Primary Industries website. 
 
What is special about soil here in Alabama? 
 
 
Alabama soil is called Bama soil. The soil has loamy subsoils. Bama 
soil has a dark brown sandy loam. Loam is a fertile soil of clay with sand, 
silt, and clay. The clay is the product of weathering. Bama soil is relatively 
highly developed and weathered and is considered to be relatively old. 
Bama soil has a lot of oxygen. Plant roots need oxygen. I got the facts from 
the Alabama Cooperative Extension System website on Google. 
 
What kind of soil does Mars have? 
 
 
Since living things do not exist on Mars, its soil does not have organic 
matter. There is no air in Martian Soil since air on Earth’s soil is specific to 
earth’s atmosphere. There is not a lot of nutrients. Martian soil is regolith. 
 
What are some facts about cucumber seeds? 
 
 
Cucumbers were thought to be poisonous when they first were 
discovered. Cucumber can be 2 feet long. They grow on vines with rough 
leaves. They thrive best at high temperatures between 75 to 85 degrees F. 
A mature cucumber ranges from 3 to 8 inches. These facts are from the 
website PA Eats. 
 
II. 
Research Question: 
• Do cucumber seeds grow/germinate better in Martian-soil or 
Earth-soil? 
 
III. 
Hypothesis: 
• If cucumber seeds are in more Earth-soil, then they will grow 
taller because Earth-soil has better nutrients (potassium, 
nitrogen, phosphorous) and Bama soil has a lot of oxygen.

Page 2 of 5 – Team Number 16385 (Fall 2023 Competition) 
 
IV. 
Variables: 
 
Independent Variable: The amount of earth and mars soil we put in the 
pots. 
Dependent Variable: How tall the plants grew. 
Control Variables: Seed type (cucumber seeds), light source, water amount 
(45 mL), and classroom temperature 
 
V. 
Procedure: 
1. Get 4 flower-pots. 
2. Label all the pots with how much Mars and Earth soil go in. 
a. 50% Bama and 50% Mars 
b. 33% Bama and 67% Mars 
c. 17% Bama and 83% Mars 
d. 0% Bama and 100% Mars 
3. Add Martian and Earth soil in all 4 pots based on what it 
says on the label. 
a. 0% = 0 Cups 
b. 17% = 1 Cup 
c. 33% = 2 Cups 
d. 50% = 3 Cups 
e. 67% = 4 Cups 
f. 83% = 5 Cups 
g. 100% = 6 Cups 
4. Put 1 cucumber seed in each pot. 
5. Turn on the plant-lights. 
6. Put one-half of a dixie cup in each flower pot every day. That 
is equal to 45 mL of water. 
7. Every Friday, measure the sprouts with a ruler and then put 
it back in the pot. If there is no school, then measure the 
seeds on Thursday. Then, put it back in. 
8. Record data in a table so you can make a line-graph.

The sprout in the pot with 50% of earth and 50% of mars soil pot grew the most. It was 
6.3cm in 8-weeks, so it grew 5.8cm. The seed in the mars soil pot grew the least. It 
ended at 2.2cm, which is an increase of 1.7cm. The pot with 33% Earth and 67% Mars 
soil grew 2.1cm and the pot with 17% earth and 83% mars grew 1.8cm.

VII. Conclusion: 
 
Answer to Hypothesis 
 
The cucumber seed grew the biggest in the pot that had 50% of Earth 
soil and 50% of mars soil in the pot, so our hypothesis was right because 
the cucumber seed grew the most in the pot that had the most earth soil! 
After 8 weeks, it was 6.3cm, so it grew 5.8cm. The seed in the pot with 
100% Mars soil grew the least. It ended at 2.2cm, which is an increase of 
1.7cm. 
 
What Can We Do Better Next Time? 
 
 
We could have brought the pots home on the weekends, so we can 
water them every single day. We could have planted the seeds for more 
weeks and more seeds in a pot. We could have kept the temperature 
constant by putting them where we could control the temperature. 
Sometimes we pulled the cucumber sprouts out too hard, so we should’ve 
been gentler so the roots didn’t break before we measured with a ruler. 
 
Teamwork 
 
 
Teamwork means working together, cooperating, helping, everyone 
having a turn, and having fun. It was fun working as a team!
